canvas.label: LED canvas
canvas.emptyZones: Zones with no LEDs (resize them in Advanced): {zones}.
canvas.hidden: {n} unnamed LEDs are not drawn but are still sent to the device.
tool.picker.hint: Pick a colour from an LED
hw.title: Hardware mode
hw.hint: Native device modes. The device runs them on its own, chroma-desk effects are paused.
hw.savedToDevice: Mode "{mode}" applied and saved to the device.
adv.resized: Zone resized to {n} LEDs and saved.
adv.sizesHint: Zone sizes are saved and re-applied on every connection (OpenRGB forgets them on restart).
type.Speaker: Speaker
err.no_connection: Not connected to the OpenRGB server.
empty.notInstalled: OpenRGB is not installed. chroma-desk can download the official portable build for you (no admin needed).
err.server_start_failed: Could not start openrgb. Is it installed?
err.server_timeout: The OpenRGB server did not respond within 30 s.
err.no_static_color: This device does not support a fixed colour.
mode.label: Lighting mode
mode.hardwareNote: The device is running its own native mode. Switch to Effects to paint LEDs and use layers.
mode.hardwareActive: The device is running the native mode "{mode}". Switch to Effects to paint LEDs and use layers.
paint.needLayer: Painting adds your strokes to a Paint layer above the selected effect.
layers.title: Layers
layers.empty: No layers yet. Add one to get started.
layers.name: Name
all.confirmColor: This replaces the layers of every device with a single solid colour. Continue?
sync.title: Global synchronisation
sync.hint: Devices are laid out left to right in the order below; one effect runs across all of them, e.g. a wave from keyboard to fans to RAM.
sync.effectsOnly: Only devices in Effects mode take part. Their own layers are drawn on top of the global scene.
sync.confirmEnable: Devices that follow the global scene will switch to Effects mode. Continue?
status.serverDown: The OpenRGB server is not running. Retrying…
empty.errorHint: Is OpenRGB installed and running with the SDK server enabled?
empty.noDevicesHint: Is OpenRGB running? Check its logs and your i2c/udev permissions, then rescan.
err.server_down: The OpenRGB server is not running.
prof.name: Name
prof.empty: No profiles yet. Set up your lights and use “Save as…”.
prof.confirmDiscard: You have unsaved changes. Applying another profile will discard them.
prof.confirmOverwrite: A profile named "{name}" already exists. Overwrite it?
prof.confirmDelete: Delete profile "{name}"? This cannot be undone.
prof.corrupt: These profile files could not be read and were ignored: {files}
err.profile_too_new: This profile was created by a newer version of chroma-desk.
err.profile_exists: A profile with that name already exists.
toast.noTray: No system tray found: closing the window minimises it instead.
quit.confirmUnsaved: You have unsaved changes in the current profile. Quit anyway?
status.guiOpen: The OpenRGB window is open. If you use both apps at once, whichever writes last wins.
err.service_failed: Could not change the systemd service
set.autostartHint: Adds an autostart entry that launches chroma-desk hidden in the tray.
set.showPhantomsHint: OpenRGB sometimes lists the same wired device twice (for example a Logitech mouse also as “receiver”). The duplicate is hidden by default.
set.startHidden: Always start hidden in the tray
set.fpsHint: Maximum updates per second sent to each type of device. Leave empty for the default.
set.serverRunning: The OpenRGB server is running and connected.
set.serverStopped: The OpenRGB server is not running.
set.service: Keep OpenRGB running with a systemd user service
set.serviceHint: Starts “openrgb --server --startminimized” on login and restarts it on failure. Close any manually started OpenRGB first.
err.anim_too_new: This animation was created by a newer version of chroma-desk.
err.anim_builtin: Built-in animations cannot be changed. Duplicate it first.
err.anim_exists: An animation with that name already exists.
err.trigger_no_device: No device is showing an effect right now. Apply a colour or animation to a device first (Lighting → Quick), then try again.
level.label: How do you want to set the lights?
level.quick.hint: Pick a colour or a ready-made animation with one click.
level.draw.hint: Paint LEDs, make frames, paths or palettes.
level.layers.hint: Advanced: stack effects with masks and blending.
quick.hint: Pick one theme (the base look of this device), then stack any effects on top. Changing the theme keeps your effects.
quick.mineEmpty: You have no animations of your own yet. Draw one and it will show up here.
anim.compatHint: How many of the LEDs this animation uses exist on the selected device. The rest are ignored.
anim.lead: Reusable animations. Apply them to any device, edit your own, share them as files or fire them from scripts.
anim.emptyTitle: You have no animations of your own yet
anim.emptyHint: Draw frames, a path or a palette on a device, save it, and it will live here.
anim.name: Name
anim.testHint: Plays it over your lights for 3 seconds
anim.confirmAll: Apply "{name}" to every device? Their current layers will be replaced.
anim.confirmDelete: Delete the animation "{name}"? Devices using it keep playing their copy.
anim.tested: Playing on {n} device(s) for a few seconds.
draw.confirmLeave: You have unsaved changes in the animation editor. Leave anyway?
paint.help: Paint LEDs with the brush. What you paint is shown live on the device. Save it to reuse it later.
save.title: Save as animation
save.nothing: Nothing to save yet: paint some LEDs first.
layers.animOutdated: The library version of this animation changed.
layers.animMissing: Removed from the library: this layer keeps playing its saved copy.
tool.path.hint: Drag over LEDs in order to draw the route
tool.gradient.hint: Drag from A to B: LEDs get palette positions 0 → 1 along the line
pal.title: Palette
pal.addHint: Click the bar to add a colour stop
draw.kind: What do you want to draw?
draw.k.frames.hint: A flipbook: several pictures in a loop.
draw.k.path.hint: Draw a route and colours travel along it.
draw.k.palette.hint: Paint a shape with a gradient that rotates.
draw.emptyHint: Paint at least one LED to enable Apply and Save.
draw.lost: {n} LED(s) of this animation do not exist on this device and were left out.
frames.help: Pick a frame, paint it, add the next one. Press Play to watch the loop. Left/Right arrow keys move between frames.
frames.lastOne: An animation needs at least one frame.
path.help: Choose the Path tool and drag across the LEDs in the order you want. A gradient will travel along the route.
cells.help: Select the LEDs that make up your shape (or leave none selected for all), then drag from A to B with the Gradient tool. The colours rotate through the palette.
trg.title: Triggers (notifications)
trg.hint: Make your lights react to anything: a script, a game mod, a cron job. A trigger plays an animation over your lights for a few seconds and then your scene comes back. Only devices in Effects mode take part.
trg.socket: From a script (local socket, JSON lines)
trg.socketHint: The socket is private to your user (mode 0600) and never listens on the network. Fields: animation, device, keys, duration, color, repeat, priority.
tour.quick.title: Start with Quick
tour.quick.text: Open any device and pick a colour or a ready-made animation. One click and your lights change.
tour.draw.title: Draw your own
tour.draw.text: In Draw you can paint LEDs, make a flipbook of frames, trace a path for colours to travel along, or paint a shape with a rotating gradient.
tour.library.title: Keep them in the library
tour.library.text: Everything you save lives in Animations: reuse it on any device, share it as a file, or trigger it from scripts when something happens.
err.profile_builtin: Built-in profiles are read-only. Duplicate it to edit.
err.profile_disabled: This built-in profile is switched off. Enable it in Profiles first.
err.profile_unavailable: This profile needs a desktop that was not detected: {detail}
err.hook_failed: Could not change the Omarchy hook: {detail}
cp.label: Colour
cp.unlinkHint: A custom colour stays the same when the theme changes.
err.palette_source: Could not read the theme: {detail}. Keeping the last good palette.
prof.disabledHint: Switched off: enable it to apply it. It follows your Omarchy theme and recolours the lights when it changes.
theme.title: Theme of {name}
theme.readOnly: Built-in profiles are read-only. Duplicate it to change its colours.
theme.fromGame: Sent by a game or script
theme.slotsDynamic: These colours come from the source ({name}) and change with it.
theme.overridesHint: Pin a slot to a fixed colour on top of any source, for example alert always pure red.
theme.presetsHint: Shown first in Quick while this profile is active.
theme.notificationsHint: {n} notification(s) in this profile. They recolour with the theme.
src.manual.hint: The colours below are this profile's own. Edit them freely.
src.omarchy.hint: Follows your current Omarchy theme: the lights change when you switch theme.
src.kde.hint: Reads the KDE Plasma colour scheme (kdeglobals).
src.pywal.hint: Reads the pywal palette (~/.cache/wal/colors.json): XFCE, i3, sway and others.
src.gtk.hint: Uses the GNOME accent colour and light/dark scheme.
src.external.hint: A game or script sends the colours with chroma-desk palette set or the socket.
themes.title: Themes
themes.hint: Lights can follow your desktop theme. Each profile chooses where its colours come from (Profiles → Theme).
themes.error: Could not read the theme source: {detail}. The last good palette is kept.
themes.rulesHint: When your Omarchy theme changes to the one on the left, the profile on the right is applied.
themes.hookHint: chroma-desk already watches Omarchy's theme files. This optional hook also pings the app right after a theme switch, as a safety net. Nothing is installed unless you press Install.
themes.noOmarchy: Omarchy was not detected on this system.
notif.lead: Notifications make your lights react: a flash when a message arrives, a red blink when your battery is low, a pulse when a build finishes. Create one, choose what it shows and where, and say what fires it.
notif.scopeProfile: New notifications belong to the profile {name}, so they recolour with its theme. You can also make them available in all profiles.
notif.scopeGlobalOnly: There is no editable profile active (save your lights as a profile to keep notifications inside it). Notifications are available in all profiles.
notif.emptyHint: Start from a template with one click, then adjust it.
notif.name: Name
notif.nameHint: Lowercase letters, numbers, - and _ (up to 32). This is the name scripts use: chroma-desk trigger <name>.
notif.badName: Use lowercase letters, numbers, - and _ (1 to 32 characters).
notif.builtinLocked: This notification belongs to a built-in profile (read-only). Use “Duplicate to edit” in Profiles, or create your own.
notif.nameTaken: There is already a notification called “{name}” there. Pick another name.
notif.needProfile: Save your lights as a profile first, or choose “All profiles”.
notif.fromLibrary: Or an animation from your library
notif.keysHint: Click the keys of {name} that should light up. Drag to select several, or use the groups.
notif.colourHint: Linked colours such as @alert follow the profile's theme: the notification recolours when the theme changes.
notif.stack: Stack on top of the previous one
notif.src.commandHint: Always available. Copy one of these into a script, a game launcher or a key binding.
notif.src.desktopHint: Fire when an application shows a desktop notification, for example Discord or Telegram.
notif.listen: Listen to desktop notifications (off by default)
notif.privacy: Privacy: chroma-desk only reads the application name, the urgency and the title of each notification to compare them with your rules. The message text is never read, stored or sent anywhere.
notif.src.omarchyHint: Omarchy tells chroma-desk through hooks. Installing one copies a small script into ~/.config/omarchy/hooks; you can remove it here at any time.
notif.hookWhat: Show exactly what will be installed
notif.hookWill: This script is copied to {path} by running:
notif.tpl.flash_all.hint: A quick flash on every device.
notif.tpl.alert_wasd.hint: W A S D blink in the alert colour.
notif.tpl.low_battery.hint: Warns when Omarchy reports low battery.
notif.tpl.desktop.hint: Flashes whenever an app shows a notification.
notif.tpl.low_health.hint: WASD blink red; a game fires it by name.
auto.lead: Automations make your lights react or show live information: a chat message blinks and orbits your keys, the F-row fills with your GPU memory, the keyboard turns red when Claude needs you. Start from a template, then change when and where it runs.
auto.pausedBanner: {n} always-on automation(s) paused by Stop all. Disabling and re-enabling or editing one also resumes it.
auto.stopHint: Ends everything showing now and pauses always-on automations until you press Resume.
auto.created: Automation “{name}” added and active. Press Test to preview it, Edit to change keys, colours or when it runs.
auto.emptyHint: Pick a template to start: a system monitor, a chat notification or an AI alert.
auto.mode.animation.hint: One flash, pulse or library animation
auto.mode.sequence.hint: Live meters (CPU, GPU, RAM), blinks, orbits, one after another
auto.keysPerStep: In a sequence every step has its own keys: pick them in the steps list above.
auto.when.lead: Switch on one or more triggers. The command is always available.
auto.when.alwaysHint: Plays in a loop on top of your lights for as long as it is enabled. Best for monitors.
auto.when.everyHint: Shows up every so often for a few seconds.
auto.when.threshold: When a value crosses a limit
auto.when.thresholdHint: Fires when a measurement stays above or below a limit, for example CPU temperature over 80 °C.
auto.when.hysteresisHint: After firing it re-arms only when the value moves back this far past the limit.
auto.when.appsHint: Several apps: separate with commas (element, fractal).
auto.when.aiHint: Fires when an AI assistant asks for your attention: permission prompts, finished work, questions.
claude.title: AI assistants
claude.lead: Light your keyboard when Claude Code needs approval or is waiting for you. This adds a Notification hook to Claude Code's settings.json that runs chroma-desk.
claude.invalid: settings.json is not valid JSON, so it was left untouched. Fix it first.
claude.show: Show exactly what will be added
claude.willAdd: This is merged into {path}; nothing else in the file changes:
claude.safe: A backup copy is made first (settings.json.chroma-desk-backup). You can remove the hook here at any time.
claude.otherHint: Run this command from any tool's notification or hook setting:
claude.clearHint: chroma-desk event ai:clear ends the alert early, for example from a hook that runs when you answer.
mon.title: Monitor
mon.lead: Readings used by meters and thresholds. Sensors are only read while a monitor is on screen or running; with none, nothing is sampled.
mon.cost: Reads twice a second while in use and stops a few seconds after the last monitor goes away.
err.claude_settings_invalid: Claude Code's settings.json is not valid or has an unexpected shape; it was not changed.
seq.minHint: the bar is empty at this value
seq.maxHint: the bar is full at this value
seq.maxHintTemp: the bar is full at this temperature
seq.holdHint: Switches the keys off for a moment: use it to end a sequence.
seq.keysMeter: A meter fills the keys in the order you pick them: first key = first bar segment.
seq.keysOrbit: The light travels the keys in the order you pick them.
seq.keysOptional: Leave the keys empty to use the whole keyboard.
seq.pickHint: Click the keys of {name} one by one, in the order you want. Numbers show the order.
seq.noKeyboard: Choose a device with a keyboard to pick keys and see the preview.
notif.tpl.gpu_monitor.hint: VRAM in green, then GPU usage in white, filling Esc to F12.
notif.tpl.cpu_monitor.hint: CPU usage in orange, then temperature in red along the number row.
notif.tpl.discord.hint: WASD and arrows blink violet 5×, orbit once, then switch off.
notif.tpl.matrix.hint: The same in Element green; also Fractal, nheko and Cinny.
notif.tpl.ai_needs_you.hint: The whole keyboard flashes the alert colour when an AI assistant needs you.
notif.tpl.gpu_temp_monitor.hint: GPU temperature in red, then GPU usage in white, filling Esc to F12.
mon.alwaysHint: The monitor stays on top of your lights all the time.
mon.periodicHint: It appears every so often and hides again after a few seconds.
mon.timingError: The visible time cannot be longer than the period, and both must be above zero.
mon.metricsHint: Pick the measurements to show, one after another. Colours and keys are set per measurement below.
anim.autosLead: Your own notifications and monitors (all profiles and the current profile). Their sequences live here too.
anim.autosEmpty: You have not created any automation yet. Make one in Automations.
anim.autosSeqSaved: Sequence saved to the library as "{name}".
quick.themesHint: The base look. One at a time: picking another replaces it.
quick.effectsHint: Overlays that stack on any theme. Click to turn on or off.
quick.roleThemeHint: Base look: appears under Themes in Quick (one at a time).
quick.roleEffectHint: Overlay: appears under Effects in Quick and stacks on any theme.
